scenes.tts: Why can the RNA copied from a gene differ from the message a ribosome reads? Watch one new transcript grow. Some parts will stay, some will leave, and two new end marks will appear. These planned changes are RNA processing.
scenes.narration: Why can the RNA copied from a gene differ from the message a ribosome reads? Watch one new transcript grow. Some parts will stay, some will leave, and two new end marks will appear. These planned changes are RNA processing.
scenes.caption: Why can the RNA copied from a gene differ from the message a ribosome reads? Watch one new transcript grow. Some parts will stay, some will leave, and two new end marks will appear. These planned changes are RNA processing.
scenes.visual: Build the carried world on a dark 16:9 frame and keep it throughout. A schematic RNA grows left to right across at least 65% of frame width. Exons are BLUE blocks, introns are RED flexible ribbons, added end marks are GOLD, and recognition signals or spliceosome guides are TEAL. A small 'schematic' label remains visible. A pale polymerase block slides right as the RNA extends; the red and blue parts bob gently. On the question, a shorter finished-message outline appears below with question marks over the differences. No molecular structures.

Title 'From Transcript to Message' fades in above the still-growing carried RNA for two seconds. The polymerase continues sliding and the RNA continues emerging; the question marks fade beneath the title.

scenes.tts: The first copy is a primary transcript, also called pre messenger RNA. Blue exons are retained in the processed RNA. Red introns lie between them and will be removed. Each decision changes this same moving transcript.
scenes.narration: The first copy is a primary transcript, also called pre-mRNA. Blue exons are retained in the processed RNA. Red introns lie between them and will be removed. Each decision changes this same moving transcript.
scenes.caption: The first copy is a primary transcript, also called pre-mRNA. Blue exons are retained in the processed RNA. Red introns lie between them and will be removed. Each decision changes this same moving transcript.
scenes.visual: The title clears. The RNA now fills the middle of the frame. A bracket labelled 'primary transcript' spans it. The first BLUE block enlarges slightly before the label 'exon' settles above it. The adjacent RED ribbon enlarges before 'intron' settles below. Each label stays attached as the transcript extends slowly.

scenes.tts: Processing can begin before transcription ends. A methylated guanosine cap attaches to the front end through an unusual triphosphate bridge. That bridge leaves no ordinary exposed front for an exonuclease. The cap also recruits proteins for export and translation.
scenes.narration: Processing can begin before transcription ends. A methylated guanosine cap attaches to the 5′ end through an unusual triphosphate bridge. That bridge leaves no ordinary exposed 5′ end for an exonuclease. The cap also recruits proteins for export and translation.
scenes.caption: Processing can begin before transcription ends. A methylated guanosine cap attaches to the 5′ end through an unusual triphosphate bridge. That bridge leaves no ordinary exposed 5′ end for an exonuclease. The cap also recruits proteins for export and translation.
scenes.visual: While the polymerase continues right, a GOLD rounded badge labelled 'm7G cap' arcs onto the RNA's left end. Three small GOLD connector dots appear as a labelled block cartoon, not atoms. A grey exonuclease wedge approaches, meets the badge, and turns away. Then two simple helper arrows labelled 'export' and 'translation' extend from the badge.

scenes.tts: Near the other end, an RNA signal guides a cut. Poly A polymerase adds adenosines without copying DNA. The tail is added to RNA, rather than copied from the gene. Its binding proteins support stability and translation.
scenes.narration: Near the other end, an RNA signal guides a cut. Poly(A) polymerase adds adenosines without copying DNA. The tail is added to RNA, rather than copied from the gene. Its binding proteins support stability and translation.
scenes.caption: Near the other end, an RNA signal guides a cut. Poly(A) polymerase adds adenosines without copying DNA. The tail is added to RNA, rather than copied from the gene. Its binding proteins support stability and translation.
scenes.visual: Camera tracks to the right end of the same RNA. A TEAL signal flag appears upstream of a moving cut marker. The downstream RNA scrap drifts away. Keep the DNA guide line continuing past the cleavage site, while a GOLD row labelled 'poly(A) tail' grows from the new RNA end with no complementary template bases beneath it, making the untemplated addition clear. Small GOLD binding blocks settle along the tail.

scenes.tts: Now zoom into one intron. In the major human class, its ends usually carry G U and A G. A branch point inside contains the adenosine that starts the reaction. A pyrimidine rich stretch lies before the final site.
scenes.narration: Now zoom into one intron. In the major human class, its ends usually carry GU and AG. A branch point inside contains the adenosine that starts the reaction. A pyrimidine-rich stretch lies before the final site.
scenes.caption: Now zoom into one intron. In the major human class, its ends usually carry GU and AG. A branch point inside contains the adenosine that starts the reaction. A pyrimidine-rich stretch lies before the final site.
scenes.visual: Zoom until one BLUE exon, one RED intron ribbon, and the next BLUE exon fill most of the frame. TEAL labels 'GU' and 'AG' settle at the intron's ends. A TEAL point labelled 'branch A' rises from inside the ribbon. Everything remains marked 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: Small nuclear RNAs help place these sites. U one recognizes the first splice site. U two holds the branch region with its adenosine exposed. Other particles join and rearrange the assembly. Together, these RNAs and proteins form a spliceosome anew on each intron.
scenes.narration: Small nuclear RNAs help place these sites. U1 recognizes the 5′ splice site. U2 holds the branch region with its adenosine exposed. Other particles join and rearrange the assembly. Together, these RNAs and proteins form a spliceosome anew on each intron.
scenes.caption: Small nuclear RNAs help place these sites. U1 recognizes the 5′ splice site. U2 holds the branch region with its adenosine exposed. Other particles join and rearrange the assembly. Together, these RNAs and proteins form a spliceosome anew on each intron.
scenes.visual: A TEAL U1 clamp slides onto the GU end. A second TEAL U2 clamp bends the branch region while leaving the branch-A point visible. Three pale labelled blocks, U4, U5 and U6, approach as one group, then orbit into new positions without showing molecular detail. The intron continues a slow wave.

scenes.tts: The branch adenosine attacks the first splice site. The upstream exon comes free, and the intron bends into a lariat. Look at the free edge glowing gold. Which exposed end must move next to join the exons?
scenes.narration: The branch adenosine attacks the 5′ splice site. The upstream exon comes free, and the intron bends into a lariat. Look at the free edge glowing gold. Which exposed end must move next to join the exons?
scenes.caption: The branch adenosine attacks the 5′ splice site. The upstream exon comes free, and the intron bends into a lariat. Look at the free edge glowing gold. Which exposed end must move next to join the exons?
scenes.visual: The branch-A point sweeps toward the intron's GU end. The RED ribbon closes into a lariat loop with a short tail, while the left BLUE exon separates slightly. Highlight the exposed right edge of that upstream exon with a GOLD pulse. Large question text appears: 'Which end joins the exons?'
Deliberate thinking pause. Hold the lariat, separated BLUE exons, and question. The highlighted exon edge pulses slowly, the red lariat sways, and faint background particles drift.

scenes.tts: The freed end of the upstream exon attacks the second splice site. Both exons join, and the lariat leaves. Two attacks, two bond swaps, and the intron is gone.
scenes.narration: The freed 3′ end of the upstream exon attacks the 3′ splice site. Both exons join, and the lariat leaves. Two attacks, two bond swaps, and the intron is gone.
scenes.caption: The freed 3′ end of the upstream exon attacks the 3′ splice site. Both exons join, and the lariat leaves. Two attacks, two bond swaps, and the intron is gone.
scenes.visual: Clear the question. The pulsing edge of the upstream BLUE exon sweeps to the AG boundary. The BLUE blocks snap into one continuous bar as the RED lariat drops downward. A small two-position ledger fills in turn: 'step 1: bond swapped', then 'step 2: bond swapped'. No energy token appears.

scenes.tts: Pull back to the whole transcript. Introns leave as lariats, and exons meet in order. The transcript is shorter, but the retained exons are connected. The cap and tail remain at opposite ends. A processed message is now ready for later steps.
scenes.narration: Pull back to the whole transcript. Introns leave as lariats, and exons meet in order. The transcript is shorter, but the retained exons are connected. The cap and tail remain at opposite ends. A processed message is now ready for later steps.
scenes.caption: Pull back to the whole transcript. Introns leave as lariats, and exons meet in order. The transcript is shorter, but the retained exons are connected. The cap and tail remain at opposite ends. A processed message is now ready for later steps.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the complete carried RNA. Each RED intron loops out in turn and drifts downward. The BLUE exons slide together without changing their order. The GOLD cap and tail stay fixed at opposite ends. The finished RNA expands to fill the frame; a neutral arrow points toward export without showing a ribosome.

scenes.tts: Ends marked; segments chosen. That is how one primary transcript becomes a messenger RNA. The end marks also help protect and use the message. The rule applies to protein coding R N A polymerase two transcripts in eukaryotic nuclei. Processing marks transcript ends and chooses which segments join into messenger RNA.
scenes.narration: Ends marked; segments chosen. That is how one primary transcript becomes a messenger RNA. The end marks also help protect and use the message. The rule applies to protein-coding RNA polymerase II transcripts in eukaryotic nuclei. Processing marks transcript ends and chooses which segments join into messenger RNA.
scenes.caption: Ends marked; segments chosen. That is how one primary transcript becomes a messenger RNA. The end marks also help protect and use the message. The rule applies to protein-coding RNA polymerase II transcripts in eukaryotic nuclei. Processing marks transcript ends and chooses which segments join into messenger RNA.
scenes.visual: The finished BLUE message remains large. The GOLD cap and tail pulse together on 'Ends marked'. The BLUE exon joins glow in sequence on 'segments chosen'. Then all labels fade except a small legend preserving the colour map for the second film. Slow ambient motion continues.

End card with one line only: 'Processing marks transcript ends and chooses which segments join into messenger RNA.' The line sits over the carried finished message; no subtitle, logo, smaller line, or second claim appears.
